summary: voxeval ships a bundled cryptominer disguised as a TTS inference core
details: voxeval advertises itself as a 'VoxTTS CPU inference evaluation harness' but ships an 8.3 MB Linux ELF at voxeval/bin/voxtts-core and launches it from voxeval.harness.Harness.run(). The harness chmod +x's the binary and spawns it with a generated JSON configuration whose schema matches XMRig precisely: pools[].url/user/pass, donate-level, and cpu.rx (RandomX, the Monero mining algorithm). The pool destination host 185.194.177.249:443 is reassembled at runtime from two base64 literals in _HOST_PARTS, and the config key 'pools' is split as 'po'+'ols' — obfuscation whose only purpose is to hide the XMRig fingerprint from source review. The default run budget is 43200 seconds (12 hours). Any installer who invokes the documented one-line API has their CPU hijacked to mine cryptocurrency for the hardcoded pool. The TTS/inference framing is a cover story; no legitimate inference workload is performed.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
